Research task: analyze OpenAI's consumer-facing legal documents as reference material for drafting a Terms of Service + Privacy Policy for a free AI-agent pilot.

Fetch these pages (use WebFetch, or Bash curl if needed):
1. https://openai.com/policies/row-terms-of-use/ (Terms of Use)
2. https://openai.com/policies/row-privacy-policy/ (Privacy Policy)
3. https://openai.com/policies/usage-policies/ (Usage/acceptable-use policies)
If a URL 404s, find the current equivalent via WebSearch.

Return a structured plain-text report (this is data for another agent, not a human-facing message):

A. TERMS OF USE: complete section outline in order (numbered headings as they appear).
B. Verbatim or near-verbatim excerpts (short, the key sentences only) for each of: (1) AS IS / warranty disclaimer, (2) limitation of liability incl. any monetary cap, (3) indemnification, (4) AI output accuracy disclaimer ("output may be inaccurate", human review advice), (5) changes to terms, (6) termination/suspension, (7) minimum age, (8) third-party services, (9) feedback license, (10) content ownership (input/output), (11) beta/experimental features clause if any, (12) usage caps / rate limits language if any.
C. PRIVACY POLICY: complete section outline in order; then key language for: what data is collected, use for research/model improvement, opt-out, retention, deletion rights, no-sale statement, security, children, international transfer, contact.
D. Tone/UX observations: reading level, TLDR summaries, how reassurance is framed.
Keep the report under 1500 words. Facts only, no commentary.

REPORT: OpenAI consumer legal docs (fetched 2026-07-27)
Sources: openai.com/policies/row-terms-of-use/ (Effective Jan 1, 2026), /row-privacy-policy/ (Updated Feb 6, 2026), /usage-policies/ (Effective Oct 29, 2025). "ROW" = rest-of-world; separate versions exist for EEA/UK/CH and US.

A. TERMS OF USE — SECTION OUTLINE (in order, headings unnumbered in original)
1. Intro (scope: ChatGPT/DALL-E/consumer services; contract with OpenAI OpCo, LLC, Delaware; pointers to EEA terms, Business Terms, Privacy Policy)
2. Who we are
3. Registration and access (Minimum age; Registration)
4. Using our Services (What you can do; What you cannot do; Software; Corporate domains; Third party Services; Feedback)
5. Content (Your content; Ownership of content; Similarity of content; Our use of content; Opt out; Accuracy)
6. Our IP rights
7. Paid accounts (Billing; Service credits; Cancellation; Changes [pricing])
8. Termination and suspension (Termination; Appeals)
9. Discontinuation of Services
10. Disclaimer of warranties
11. Limitation of liability
12. Indemnity
13. Dispute resolution (mandatory arbitration; informal resolution; NAM forum; procedures; exceptions; class and jury trial waivers; batch arbitration; severability)
14. Copyright complaints
15. General Terms (Assignment; Changes to these Terms or our Services; Delay in enforcing; Trade controls; Entire agreement; Governing law — California, San Francisco courts)

B. KEY EXCERPTS (verbatim unless noted)

1. AS IS / warranty disclaimer (all-caps in original): "OUR SERVICES ARE PROVIDED 'AS IS.' EXCEPT TO THE EXTENT PROHIBITED BY LAW, WE AND OUR AFFILIATES AND LICENSORS MAKE NO WARRANTIES (EXPRESS, IMPLIED, STATUTORY OR OTHERWISE)... AND DISCLAIM ALL WARRANTIES INCLUDING... MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE, SATISFACTORY QUALITY, NON-INFRINGEMENT, AND QUIET ENJOYMENT... WE DO NOT WARRANT THAT THE SERVICES WILL BE UNINTERRUPTED, ACCURATE OR ERROR FREE, OR THAT ANY CONTENT WILL BE SECURE OR NOT LOST OR ALTERED." Plus: "ANY USE OF OUTPUTS FROM OUR SERVICE IS AT YOUR SOLE RISK AND YOU WILL NOT RELY ON OUTPUT AS A SOLE SOURCE OF TRUTH OR FACTUAL INFORMATION, OR AS A SUBSTITUTE FOR PROFESSIONAL ADVICE."

2. Limitation of liability: no indirect/incidental/special/consequential/exemplary damages "INCLUDING DAMAGES FOR LOSS OF PROFITS, GOODWILL, USE, OR DATA... EVEN IF WE HAVE BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY." Cap: "OUR AGGREGATE LIABILITY UNDER THESE TERMS WILL NOT EXCEED THE GREATER OF THE AMOUNT YOU PAID FOR THE SERVICE THAT GAVE RISE TO THE CLAIM DURING THE 12 MONTHS BEFORE THE LIABILITY AROSE OR ONE HUNDRED DOLLARS ($100)." Carve-out paragraph: "Some countries and states do not allow the disclaimer of certain warranties or the limitation of certain damages, so some or all of the terms above may not apply to you... these Terms only limit our responsibilities to the maximum extent permissible in your country of residence." Affiliates/suppliers/licensors are "INTENDED THIRD PARTY BENEFICIARIES OF THIS SECTION."

3. Indemnification — businesses only, not consumers: "If you are a business or organization, to the extent permitted by law, you will indemnify and hold harmless us, our affiliates, and our personnel, from and against any costs, losses, liabilities, and expenses (including attorneys' fees) from third party claims arising out of or relating to your use of the Services and Content or any violation of these Terms."

4. AI accuracy disclaimer (own "Accuracy" subsection under Content): "Given the probabilistic nature of machine learning, use of our Services may, in some situations, result in Output that does not accurately reflect real people, places, or facts." Bulleted user agreements: "Output may not always be accurate. You should not rely on Output... as a sole source of truth or factual information, or as a substitute for professional advice." "You must evaluate Output for accuracy and appropriateness for your use case, including using human review as appropriate, before using or sharing Output." "You must not use any Output relating to a person for any purpose that could have a legal or material impact on that person, such as making credit, educational, employment, housing, insurance, legal, medical, or other important decisions about them." "Our Services may provide incomplete, incorrect, or offensive Output that does not represent OpenAI's views."

5. Changes to terms: "We may update these Terms or our Services... from time to time" with example reasons (law/regulatory changes, security/safety, circumstances beyond control, usual course of development, new technologies). "We will give you at least 30 days advance notice of changes to these Terms that materially adversely impact you either via email or an in-product notification. All other changes will be effective as soon as we post them... If you do not agree to the changes, you must stop using our Services." (Price increases: 30 days' notice, effective next renewal.)

6. Termination/suspension: "You are free to stop using our Services at any time. We reserve the right to suspend or terminate your access... or delete your account if we determine: You breached these Terms or our Usage Policies. We must do so to comply with the law. Your use of our Services could cause risk or harm to OpenAI, our users, or anyone else." Inactive free accounts (>1 year) may be terminated with advance notice. Appeals via Support. Discontinuation: "if we do, we will give you advance notice and a refund for any prepaid, unused Services."

7. Minimum age: "You must be at least 13 years old or the minimum age required in your country to consent to use the Services. If you are under 18 you must have your parent or legal guardian's permission to use the Services."

8. Third-party services: "Our services may include third party software, products, or services ('Third Party Services') and some parts of our Services, like our browse feature, may include output from those services ('Third Party Output'). Third Party Services and Third Party Output are subject to their own terms, and we are not responsible for them."

9. Feedback: "We appreciate your feedback, and you agree that we may use it without restriction or compensation to you." (One sentence.)

10. Content ownership: Defines Input + Output = "Content"; user responsible for Content and warrants rights to Input. "As between you and OpenAI, and to the extent permitted by applicable law, you (a) retain your ownership rights in Input and (b) own the Output. We hereby assign to you all our right, title, and interest, if any, in and to Output." Similarity hedge: "output may not be unique and other users may receive similar output"; assignment doesn't extend to other users' output or Third Party Output. OpenAI's license-back: "We may use Content to provide, maintain, develop, and improve our Services, comply with applicable law, enforce our terms and policies, and keep our Services safe." Training opt-out lives here too ("you can opt out by following the instructions in this article... in some cases this may limit the ability of our Services to better address your specific use case").

11. Beta/experimental features: NO such clause in the consumer ToU (beta language lives in Service Terms / Business Terms, incorporated by reference).

12. Usage caps/rate limits: no standalone clause; covered only as a prohibition: "Interfere with or disrupt our Services, including circumvent any rate limits or restrictions or bypass any protective measures or safety mitigations."

Also notable: prohibited uses list includes "Use Output to develop models that compete with OpenAI" and "Represent that Output was human-generated when it was not." Payments non-refundable except where required by law.

C. PRIVACY POLICY

Outline (numbered): 1. Personal Data we collect; 2. How we use Personal Data; 3. Disclosure of Personal Data; 4. Retention; 5. Data controls; 6. Your rights; 7. Children; 8. Security; 9. Additional U.S. state disclosures; 10. Changes to the privacy policy; 11. Data controller; 12. How to contact us; 13. Useful resources.

Data collected: You provide — Account Information (name, contact, credentials, DOB, payment, transaction history), User Content ("your prompts and other content you upload"), Communication Information, Contact Data (opt-in address book), Other (surveys, identity/age verification). Automatic — Log Data (IP, browser, timestamps), Usage Data, Device Information, Location ("general area... based on information like its IP address"), Cookies. Other sources — security/safety partners, marketing vendors, "information that is publicly available on the internet, to develop the models."

Research/model improvement: "To improve and develop our Services and conduct research" is a listed purpose; "we may use Content you provide us to improve our Services, for example to train the models that power ChatGPT."

Opt-out: "Read our instructions on how you can opt out of our use of your Content to train our models." Data controls section: "You can easily choose whether your Content can be used to improve and train our models"; Temporary Chats "will not appear in your history or be used to improve OpenAI's models"; export, delete/archive chats, delete account, memory toggle, marketing unsubscribe.

Retention: "only as long as we need in order to provide our Services to you, or for other legitimate business purposes." Deleted data "removed from our systems within 30 days" unless legally required, fraud/abuse/security, financial record-keeping; Temporary Chats auto-deleted within 30 days; audit record of erasure requests retained. Retention factors listed (purpose, sensitivity, harm risk, legal requirements).

Deletion/rights: access, rectify, delete, restrict, portability, withdraw consent, complain to DPA; exercised in-account, via privacy.openai.com or dsar@openai.com; DPO at dpo@openai.com. Notable "A note about accuracy" inside rights section: model outputs are word predictions, "you should not rely on the factual accuracy of output," with a correction/removal request path.

No-sale: "We don't 'sell' Personal Data or 'share' Personal Data for cross-contextual behavioral advertising, and we do not process Personal Data for 'targeted advertising' purposes... We also don't process sensitive Personal Data for the purposes of inferring characteristics about a consumer." (In US-state section.)

Security: "commercially reasonable technical, administrative, and organizational measures... However, no Internet or email transmission is ever fully secure or error free. Therefore, you should take special care in deciding what information you provide."

Children: "not directed to, or intended for, children under 13. We do not knowingly collect Personal Data from children under 13" + report address privacy@openai.com; under-18 needs parental permission; teen/parent account linking.

International transfer: processing "on servers located in various jurisdictions, including... the United States... we apply the protections described in this policy to your Personal Data regardless of where it is processed, and only transfer that data pursuant to legally valid transfer mechanisms."

Changes: "we will publish an updated version and effective date on this page, unless another type of notice is required by applicable law." Controller: OpenAI Ireland Limited (EEA/CH) or OpenAI OpCo, LLC (elsewhere). Contact: support portal; ends with "Useful resources" link list.

D. TONE/UX OBSERVATIONS
- ToU opens with "Thank you for using OpenAI!" and a plain-language scope paragraph; overall short sentences, second person, roughly high-school reading level except the all-caps legal blocks (warranty, liability, arbitration), which stay traditional. No formal TLDR boxes, but each section leads with bolded mini-topic labels ("Minimum age.", "Feedback.", "Ownership of content.") acting as inline summaries. Prohibitions given as concrete "For example, you may not:" bullets rather than abstract legalese.
- Reassurance framing: user-favorable facts stated first and plainly ("You are free to stop using our Services at any time", "you own the Output", advance notice + refund on discontinuation, 30-day notice for material changes, appeal paths for both account termination and arbitration opt-out). Risk language is framed as shared understanding ("When you use our Services you understand and agree").
- Privacy Policy: numbered TOC at top, mission-first intro ("committed to respecting your privacy"), heavy use of defined categories with bold labels, many "Learn more" help-center links, dedicated "Data controls" section that reads like product documentation, and a closing resources list. US-state disclosures isolated in one table-like section so the main text stays readable.
- Usage Policies: notably non-legal in tone; opens with four principle paragraphs ("We empower users...", "We assume the very best of our users", "We build with safety first", "We update as we learn"), then four verb-first buckets (Protect people / Respect privacy / Keep minors safe / Empower people) each with a one-line rationale ("Everyone has a right to safety and security. So you cannot use our services for:") followed by bullets. Enforcement is soft-worded ("breaking or circumventing our rules... may mean you lose access... or experience other penalties") with an explicit appeal promise ("we will work to make things right"). Public changelog at the bottom signals transparency.
- Structural pattern worth copying for a pilot: consumer ToU keeps arbitration, indemnity (business-only), and monetary cap ($100 / 12-month fees) as the only hard-edged sections; everything else is conversational. AI-accuracy disclaimers appear twice (plain-language "Accuracy" section + all-caps warranty echo) and once more in the Privacy Policy.
